title: fix(schemas): canonicalize phase-graph node IDs and guard them
body:
<!-- idd-skill-authoring-publication: target=target-f1c954422d68a288; anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#3026; set=set-d9ac57f123437ad6; session=claude-idd-authoring-3405aa6f371d; token=pub-b56c9a50b39e2cfc -->

## Background

Parent roadmap: #3026

`src/scripts/phase-id-resolver.mts` declares the canonical machine-facing
phase IDs (`DEFAULT_CANONICAL_PHASE_IDS`, 47 entries) and a legacy-alias
map that normalizes older spellings onto them — `F2_5` accepts `F2.5`,
`F2-5`, and `F25`; `A4_5` accepts `A4.5`, `A4-5`, and `A45`.

`schemas/phase-graph.json` is the machine-readable routing graph, validated
for referential integrity by `src/scripts/validate-schemas.mts`. Comparing
its node IDs against the resolver's canonical list:

- the graph declares a node `F2.5`, which is a **legacy alias**, not the
  canonical `F2_5`. The same string also appears inside `F2`'s `next`
  array.
- the graph has 38 nodes against 47 canonical IDs. Eleven canonical IDs are
  absent: `A0`, `A0_O`, `A0_T`, `A1`, `A1_5`, `A2`, `A3`, `A3_5`, `A4`,
  `A4_5`, and `F2_5`.
- the graph declares a bare `A` node that is not a canonical phase ID.

The bare `A` node is deliberate and documented: the resolver's own header
comment states it is "the collapsed routing-graph-only node in
`schemas/phase-graph.json`", `resume-route-selection` never emits it, and
`tests/phase-id-resolver.test.mts` asserts `A` resolves to
`unknown_phase_id`. Whether to expand it into the concrete discovery
sub-phases is a routing-model decision, not a naming defect, and it is out
of scope here.

The `F2.5` node is a different matter. It is a naming inconsistency between
two files that are supposed to share one vocabulary, and nothing today
prevents it or the next one: no check asserts that a graph node ID is a
canonical phase ID. Today the inconsistency is latent rather than live —
grepping `src/` and `tests/` finds no consumer that looks a resolver-
produced canonical ID up in the graph — but it means the graph cannot be
trusted as the substrate for any phase re-ordering work until both the
spelling and the guard exist. This is preventive; no incident is attributed
to it.

## Proposed change

- Rename the `schemas/phase-graph.json` node `F2.5` to the canonical
  `F2_5`, including the occurrence inside `F2`'s `next` array. Do not
  change any edge, and do not add or remove any node.
- Add a test asserting that every `schemas/phase-graph.json` node ID is
  either a canonical phase ID per `phase-id-resolver` or the documented
  collapsed `A` node, and that no node ID is a legacy alias of a canonical
  ID. The `A` exemption must be explicit and commented, naming the resolver
  comment it mirrors, so a future reader can tell a deliberate exemption
  from an unnoticed gap.
- Leave `tests/phase-id-resolver.test.mts`'s existing
  `assertUnknownPhaseId('A')` assertion unchanged; it and the new test
  encode the same decision from opposite directions.

Do not expand the collapsed `A` node, do not renumber any phase, and do not
touch the legacy-alias map. Those belong to the re-order proposal this
track's sibling issue produces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `schemas/phase-graph.json` contains no node ID and no `next` entry
      spelled `F2.5`; the node and its inbound edge read `F2_5`.
- [ ] The graph's node count and edge set are otherwise byte-for-byte
      unchanged apart from that rename; state this explicitly in the PR
      body.
- [ ] A test fails when a node ID is introduced that is neither a canonical
      phase ID nor the documented `A` node.
- [ ] That same test fails when a node ID is changed to a legacy alias of a
      canonical ID, for example reverting `F2_5` to `F2.5`.
- [ ] The `A` exemption in that test carries a comment naming the
      `phase-id-resolver` header comment that documents the collapse.
- [ ] `node --test tests/*.test.mts` passes, including the existing
      referential-integrity validation of the live graph data file.
- [ ] The full `pre-push-validate` command from the Project commands table
      passes.

## Candidate files

- `schemas/phase-graph.json`
- `tests/phase-id-resolver.test.mts`
- `tests/schema-validation.test.mts`
- `src/scripts/phase-id-resolver.mts`

---

_Autopilot suitability: 5 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable; below
the configured floor is human-oriented. A one-token rename plus a test,
with the one judgment call (whether to expand the collapsed node) removed
from scope and assigned to the sibling issue._
